title: AI-credit reservation leak in the single-file AI-upload path — `reserve()` is called outside any try/catch, so a downstream throw in `Evidence.create`/`debugLog`/`assignEvidenceCode` never commits or cancels the reservation
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js` — `uploadAI` handler (single-file AI-assisted upload, `POST /upload/ai`)
**Root Cause:** `aiUploadBilling.reserve(req.orgId, evidenceId, aiUploadConfig)` is called at line 788, OUTSIDE any try/catch block. The following code — `Evidence.create(...)` (lines 794-828), `debugLog(...)` (lines 830-838), and `assignEvidenceCode(...)` (line 840) — is also NOT wrapped in try/catch. Only `queueUploadJobs`/`commitSuccessful`/`cancelFailed` (lines 858-891) are inside a try/catch that correctly commits or cancels the reservation. Contrast with the bulk-upload path (`uploadAIBulk`, lines 927-1075) where `reserve()` at line 976 IS inside the same try block that also contains `Evidence.create` and `assignEvidenceCode`, with `cancelFailed` in the catch (lines 1058-1069) — the single-file path is inconsistent with its own bulk sibling.
**Impact:** If `Evidence.create` throws (Mongoose validation error, duplicate key, transient Mongo error) after the credit reservation at line 788 succeeds, the reservation is never committed (no charge, so no evidence produced) NOR cancelled (so the hold is never released) — the customer's AI-upload allowance/credit balance is permanently strand-held for work that never happened, a real entitlement/billing integrity bug that would surface as customers losing AI credits with no matching evidence record to show for it.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js — uploadAI handler

1. Wrap the reserve() call and everything through Evidence.create/debugLog/assignEvidenceCode in one try/catch, mirroring the uploadAIBulk pattern (lines 971-1074).
2. In the catch, call aiUploadBilling.cancelFailed(aiCreditReservationId) before re-throwing/responding with the error.
3. Add a regression test: mock Evidence.create to throw, assert cancelFailed is called with the reservation id from reserve().
```

title: Presigned-upload confirm path bypasses magic-byte content validation — declared `mimeType` is trusted with no inspection of the actual uploaded S3 object bytes, unlike the direct multipart upload path
description:
**Files:** `evidence-upload.controller.js:1713-1751` (`generateUploadUrl`, `POST /upload/presigned`), `:1757-1817` (`confirmPresignedUpload`, `POST /:evidenceId/files/confirm`); `evidence-upload.routes.js:79-87,120-129` (neither route has `validateMagicBytes` attached); `evidence-upload.multer.js:96-117` (`validateMagicBytes` — the magic-byte check that IS attached to every direct multer route)
**Root Cause:** The direct multipart upload path (`multerUpload`/`multerSingle` + `validateMagicBytes`, attached on every route in `evidence-upload.routes.js` lines 58/72/73/76/132) inspects the first 4100 bytes of every uploaded file against `ALLOWED_DETECTED_MIMES` — specifically to defend against a file claiming an allowed MIME type while actually containing disallowed content (the multer.js file's own comment explains this is exactly why `application/octet-stream` is excluded: "any file can claim this type"). The presigned-upload flow has no equivalent check: `generateUploadUrl` validates the CLIENT-DECLARED `mimeType` against `ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES` (line 1719-1724, correctly excluding text/html etc.) before issuing the presigned URL, but the client then uploads the actual file bytes directly to S3 — bypassing the application entirely — and `confirmPresignedUpload` only verifies file SIZE via an S3 HEAD request (lines 1775-1783); it never downloads or inspects the object's actual bytes. The `mimeType` stored on `evidence.files[]` (line 1795: `mimeType: mimeType || s3Meta.contentType`) is whatever the client declared, not a magic-byte-verified value.
**Impact:** A malicious client can request a presigned URL declaring an allowed mimeType (e.g. `application/pdf`), then PUT arbitrary byte content (e.g. an HTML payload) to S3 with a `Content-Type: application/pdf` header satisfying the presign signature — content the multer path's magic-byte check would have rejected — and it becomes a confirmed evidence file with no server-side content verification at any point. Files can later be served `inline` (confirmed at `evidence.controller.js:898` and `evidence-upload.controller.js:1524`), so a content-type/content mismatch is a meaningful defense-in-depth gap versus the multer path's documented threat model.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js — confirmPresignedUpload

1. After the existing S3 HEAD/size check, download the first ~4KB of the object (S3 GetObject with a Range header) and run it through the same fileTypeFromBuffer + ALLOWED_DETECTED_MIMES check used by validateMagicBytes in evidence-upload.multer.js.
2. If the detected type is disallowed, delete the S3 object and the TenantStorageObject reservation (mirroring the existing size-mismatch rejection path at lines 1779-1783) and return 400.
3. Extract the magic-byte check in evidence-upload.multer.js into a reusable function callable both from validateMagicBytes (multer path) and confirmPresignedUpload (presigned path) instead of duplicating logic.
```

title: No ISO 27001 Annex A control reference per integration evidence item — `IntegrationEvidenceListPage.jsx` shows no MODEL_TO_ANNEX_A mapping; auditors cannot determine which Annex A control each integration evidence satisfies
description:
**Files:** all 10 provider renderers under `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/integration-hub/evidence-detail/` (GitHubEvidenceContent.jsx, JiraEvidenceContent.jsx, NessusEvidenceContent.jsx, OpenVASEvidenceContent.jsx, Rapid7EvidenceContent.jsx, SentinelEvidenceContent.jsx, SplunkEvidenceContent.jsx, SumoLogicEvidenceContent.jsx, OktaEvidenceContent.jsx, GenericEvidenceContent.jsx)
**Root Cause:** Re-checked across all 10 provider-specific renderers (up from the original 4 documented) — a case-insensitive grep for `Annex`, `A.5`, `A.8`, `control` returns zero real Annex A control-code matches in any of them; only `Rapid7EvidenceContent.jsx` has generic prose mentions of 'controls' with no framework/control-code mapping.
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN across the now-larger 10-renderer surface. NOTE: a static, non-computed ISO 27001/SOC2/NIST mapping DOES appear in the PDF export path (`IntegrationEvidenceDetailPage.jsx:225-229`), but it is hardcoded and identical for every evidence item regardless of type — that is a distinct, worse defect tracked separately as EM-043 (fabricated compliance data), not a fix for this gap.
**Fix in progress 2026-08-29:** Implemented differently than the fix prompt below suggested. The 10 provider renderers are not standalone pages — they export Metrics/AuditorTags/RecordsTable pieces composed by IntegrationEvidenceDetailPage.jsx — so duplicating a control-mapping section into all 10 risked exactly the kind of static/duplicated-list problem EM-043 already flagged as a Critical defect. Instead: extended `IntegrationEvidenceRepository.findLatestByOrg` (vibrantix-connector-service) with a lightweight follow-up aggregate against `ext_integration_control_verdicts` (bounded to the returned page, not the fragile dedup pipeline), attaching real `mappedControls: [{frameworkName, controlStringId, controlTitle}]` per item — the SAME source IntegrationEvidenceDetailPage.jsx's own Mapped Controls panel and PDF export use. `IntegrationEvidenceListPage.jsx` now renders a 'Controls' column with a count badge + tooltip listing them, sourced from this real data, not a new static list.
**Claude Fix Prompt (original):**
```
Files: all 10 provider renderers under integration-hub/evidence-detail/

1. Add a shared MODEL_TO_ANNEX_A mapping utility (single source of truth, imported by all 10 renderers, not duplicated).
2. Add an "Annex A Controls" section/badges to each renderer using the item's canonical model/type.
3. Ensure this is sourced from the SAME real per-evidence control-verdict data already used in IntegrationEvidenceDetailPage.jsx (controlStringId/controlTitle/verdict), not a new static list — see EM-043 for why a static list is itself a Critical defect.
```

title: Export formats silently fail with generic error toast — `handleExport` catches errors with no indication which formats are implemented; auditors preparing ZIP bundles before certification get silent failures; violates Clause 7.5.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/ExportShareContent.jsx:187-218` (`handleExport`), `:376-398` (`isSupported` gate), `:583-594` (Recent Exports row Download button)
**Root Cause:** Partially improved but core gap remains. The main format-selection UI now gates unsupported formats via `isSupported = format === 'csv'` (line 376) with a 'Coming Soon' tooltip, disabling the button — this is new since the original finding. However `handleExport` itself (lines 187-218) still coerces any non-csv format to `json` (line 190) and funnels every failure into one identical `catch` block with a generic 'Export failed' toast — no distinction between 'not implemented' vs. network/server errors. Worse: the 'Recent Exports' per-row Download button (lines 583-594) calls `handleExport(format)` for ANY historical format unconditionally, completely bypassing the `isSupported` gate that protects the main UI.
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN (partial improvement in the primary flow; the history-row download bypass is arguably a new sub-issue worth explicit test coverage).
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
File: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/ExportShareContent.jsx

1. Apply the same isSupported check inside the Recent Exports row Download handler (line ~588) before calling handleExport — do not let history rows bypass the gate.
2. In handleExport's catch block, distinguish error types:
   if (err.status === 404) toast.info(`${format} export is not yet available`);
   else if (err.status === 408 || err.status === 504) toast.error('Export timed out — try a smaller date range');
   else toast.error(`Export failed: ${err.message}`);
```

title: Mandatory reviewer note missing in AI metadata validation drawer — `resolutionNotes` Textarea in `EvidenceValidationReviewDrawer.jsx` is optional with no minimum length; accepted metadata with no trail; violates ISO 19011:2018 §6.4.9
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceValidationReviewDrawer.jsx:70` (`resolutionNotes` state)
**Root Cause:** Worse than originally documented — `resolutionNotes` (line 70) is not merely 'optional', it is completely dead state: never rendered in any Textarea/FormControl, never read anywhere else in the file, and never passed to `evidenceValidationService.resolveWorkflow()` in `handleAcceptAI` (lines 146-194) or `handleSplitFiles` (lines 197-249). No input for it exists in the UI at all.
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN — confirmed the field is entirely unwired, not just unvalidated.
**Fix in progress 2026-08-29:** Frontend fully wired — Textarea added and rendered in the Accept/Split flow, ≥30-character validation gates both the toast-level check and the footer buttons' isDisabled, and resolutionNotes is now passed as a third argument through evidenceValidationService.resolveWorkflow() to the backend. IMPORTANT DISCOVERY: a repo-wide search of vibrantix-backend found NO route, controller, or model for `/evidence-validation/workflow/:id/resolve` or `/resolve-with-assignee` anywhere — this entire drawer's save actions (Accept AI Suggestions, Split to New) appear to call a backend endpoint that does not exist in this codebase, a separate and more severe pre-existing defect than this ticket describes. Not built as part of this fix — flagged for the user to decide whether it needs its own ticket and where that backend logic should actually live.
**Claude Fix Prompt (original):**
```
File: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/evidence-management/EvidenceValidationReviewDrawer.jsx

1. Add a Textarea bound to resolutionNotes, rendered in the Accept/Keep AI metadata flow.
2. In handleAcceptAI, add before the API call:
   if (!resolutionNotes || resolutionNotes.trim().length < 30) {
     setNoteError('Resolution note required (min 30 characters)'); return;
   }
3. Pass resolutionNotes into the resolveWorkflow() payload — it is currently never sent.
4. Backend AI validation endpoint: add resolutionNotes: Joi.string().min(30).required()
```

title: Google Drive Bearer token sent directly to connector service origin — JWT from `state.auth.token` in raw `fetch()` to `CS_URL` in `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx`; bypasses Next.js API proxy; CORS failure likely in production; violates A.8.20
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/services/integrationHubService.js:10-13` (`CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL`), `:29-47` (`getIntegrationHubAccessToken`), `:52-69` (axios instance + request interceptor)
**Root Cause:** The implementation has changed but the underlying defect persists in a different location. `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx` itself no longer makes a raw `fetch()` call (confirmed — zero `fetch(` occurrences); it now delegates to `getConnectors`/`getDriveFiles` from `integrationHubService.js`. That service still calls the connector-service origin DIRECTLY (`CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL`, defaulting to `http://localhost:5009/api/connector-service`) via a dedicated axios instance, bypassing any Next.js API proxy, with a request interceptor (line 64) attaching `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — the token now sourced from the NextAuth session (`getSession()`, line 34) rather than Redux state, but the direct-to-connector-service-origin, proxy-bypassing pattern is unchanged.
**Re-verified 2026-08-27:** STILL OPEN, relocated from `GDriveFileBrowser.jsx` (no longer applicable — no raw fetch there) to `integrationHubService.js` (the real current location of the bearer-token-to-connector-service-origin pattern). NOTE: separately, the specific Google Drive routes this service calls do not even exist on the connector-service side — see new Critical defect EM-042, which supersedes this as the primary blocker for the Google Drive feature specifically (this defect's security concern still applies to every other integration-hub call routed through this same service file).
**2026-08-29 assessment:** Deliberately left unfixed after review with the user. There is no Next.js API proxy anywhere in this app to "bypass" — every backend call (including the main `vibrantix-backend`, not just connector-service) is made directly from the browser with a bearer token attached client-side; this is the app's established, deliberate calling convention, not a one-off mistake in this file. connector-service's CORS allowlist (`index.ts`) already includes the real prod/dev domains, so the "CORS failure likely in production" claim is not currently substantiated. Building an isolated proxy for just this one service would be architecturally inconsistent with the rest of the app and would not meaningfully reduce token exposure (the token still has to be usable by browser JS to attach to requests either way) — a real fix would mean session-based server-side auth across the whole app, a much larger initiative than a single-file patch. Left open pending a deliberate app-wide architecture decision, not scheduled as part of this fix pass.
**Claude Fix Prompt (original):**
```
1. Create a Next.js API route (e.g. app/api/integration-hub/[...path]/route.js) that proxies requests to CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL server-side, attaching the bearer token from the server-side session rather than exposing it to a cross-origin client request.
2. In integrationHubService.js, replace the direct axios baseURL pointing at CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL with calls to the new Next.js proxy route.
3. Remove NEXT_PUBLIC_CONNECTOR_SERVICE_URL (a client-exposed env var) once no client code calls the connector service directly.
```

title: Verdict rejection silently overwritten by next AI-upload callback
fixEvidence: First formally persisted to the JSON store this run (previously documented only in this agent's own 'Known Confirmed Defects' narrative, never written to a severity file). Verified FIXED in code as of 2026-08-27: `evidence-control-verdicts.controller.js:135-165` (`reportControlVerdicts`, the AI-upload 'completed' callback) still does a full-array replace of `evidence.controlVerdicts` (line 139: `evidenceUpdate.controlVerdicts = verdicts.map(...)`), but it now explicitly builds a `priorByCode` lookup (lines 135-137) and, for any `uclCode` whose prior `reviewStatus` was not `'pending'` (i.e. previously `'approved'` or `'rejected'`), carries forward `reviewStatus`/`reviewedBy`/`reviewedAt`/`rejectionReason` from the prior record instead of resetting to `'pending'` (lines 141, 157-162). An inline comment (lines 123-134) explicitly documents this as a deliberate fix for exactly this bug: "A human review decision must survive a re-run of the pipeline. This used to hard-code reviewStatus:'pending' for every incoming verdict...". Confirmed via `git log` that this file has received targeted fix commits. No dedicated regression test exists yet for this specific preserve-on-rerun behavior — worth adding, but the production code path is confirmed correct.
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence.model.js` (`controlVerdicts[]` schema); `evidence-control-verdicts.controller.js` (AI-upload callback); `evidence-verdict-rejection.model.js` (append-only rejection log)
**Root Cause (original, as documented in this agent's architecture notes 2026-08-16):** Rejecting an AI-suggested control verdict flipped `evidence.controlVerdicts[].reviewStatus` to `'rejected'` in place, but the next AI-upload callback for that evidence item replaced the entire `controlVerdicts[]` array wholesale, silently discarding the rejection.
**Status:** FIXED — see fixEvidence. This record is being persisted to the JSON store for the first time in this run; it was previously described only in this agent's narrative documentation, never logged as a JSON defect.

title: Evidence can be uploaded and saved with zero requirement/control/UCL mapping, and nothing in the UI flags it as unmapped
description:
`createEvidence` (`vibrantix-backend/src/modules/evidence/evidence-upload.controller.js:343-551`) only requires `title`, `evidenceType`, and a file. `requirementMappings`/`directUclMappings` (lines 353-354) are optional and default to `[]`; if empty, no `EvidenceRequirementMapping`/`EvidenceUclMapping` row is ever written, yet the document is saved as real, filed evidence. Coverage is correctly computed only from evidence IDs already present in `ClientRequirement.evidenceIds`/`ClientControl.evidenceIds`, so unmapped evidence is correctly excluded from coverage math - but there is no compensating signal anywhere in the UI: `EvidenceTable.jsx` and the evidence-management component tree have no 'unmapped'/'no controls linked' badge or filter.

Auditor-facing breakage: an org can accumulate evidence that looks 'filed' in Evidence Management indefinitely with no control behind it, and nothing on the list screen tells the auditor which items these are.
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.2 documented information must indicate its nature

title: No true single-pane 'evidence by control across every source' view even within Evidence Management itself; two structurally separate mapping systems both partial
description:
The one control-centric evidence view in Evidence Management, `ControlDetailsDrawer.jsx:73-98`, calls only `evidenceService.getMappingsByControl(lookupId)`, which reads solely from the LEGACY `EvidenceControlMapping` collection. It does not query `EvidenceUclMapping`/`EvidenceRequirementMapping` (the newer, AI-verdict-fed system), nor integration evidence, cloud-posture, vendor, or policy evidence - those live on `ClientControl`'s separate `integrationEvidenceIds`/`vendorControlIds`/`policyIds`/`certificationIds`/`scannerCheckIds` arrays, which have no exposed aggregate read endpoint reachable from this drawer.

Auditor-facing breakage: two structurally separate evidence-mapping systems coexist, and the only 'view evidence for this control' screen in Evidence Management shows just one of them - an auditor picking a control here can be shown an incomplete evidence set while believing it's exhaustive.
